case.presentation: Patient is a 77-year-old man with hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes. One week ago, he awoke with sudden right-sided arm and leg weakness lasting about 30 minutes without facial droop or speech changes. He presented to a local ED the next day. CT head and MRI brain were unrevealing. His basic labs were unremarkable. Today, his ABCD2 score is 5, so I initiated dual antiplatelet therapy (aspirin 81 mg indefinitely + clopidogrel 75 mg for 21 days) and ordered a 7-day Zio patch. Does the patient need further evaluation or medication adjustments?
case.recommendations: Recommend extending ambulatory cardiac monitoring to 14 days (keep the Zio patch in place for the full duration) to maximize detection of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation; if monitoring or echocardiography reveals atrial fibrillation, transition from antiplatelet therapy to therapeutic anticoagulation. Obtain vessel imaging via CTA or MRA of head and neck; if significant carotid stenosis is identified, refer for vascular surgery or interventional evaluation for possible revascularization. Obtain a non-urgent echo. Place an urgent referral to Neurology for comprehensive stroke workup and ongoing management. Order fasting lipids and A1c with plan to intensify risk-factor control: target blood pressure < 130/80 mmHg, LDL < 70 mg/dL with annual lipid checks, and HbA1c < 7%. Counsel on Mediterranean‐style diet, at least 30 minutes of moderate exercise five days weekly, and smoking/alcohol cessation if applicable. Educate the patient on stroke warning signs (e.g., BEFAST) and to call 911 if symptoms recur. Otherwise, continue dual antiplatelet therapy as planned with aspirin indefinitely after 21 days.
